title: jtasks plan
description: The plan (or one batch of it) that `jtasks plan` / `jtasks plan --add` takes: a list of tasks, or an object with `tasks`.

feature.description: Short slug of the feature (names the run).

objective.description: One line: what the run achieves.

source.description: The spec, issue or document the plan came from (a path or a URL); every task without its own source shows it in its ticket.

profiles.description: Agent profiles by name; without it: execute, execute-deep, review.

serialize.description: Commands that must run one at a time on the machine (e.g. "bun test"); they run through jlock run.

maxAttempts.description: Attempts before a task fails (default 2). A subagent that ends without finishing does not spend one: see maxAgentEnded.

maxAgentEnded.description: Times a task's subagent may end without finishing before the task fails and the run pauses for a person (default 3).

awaitGrace.description: How long a task whose subagent ended while its process ran waits for the subagent to come back once the process ended (default 5m).

holdTtl.description: How long a task's locks live if nobody renews or gives them back, e.g. 2h (the default): the ttl of every jlock hold. The mod and the plugin renew the locks of tasks in progress, so it only frees a window that died.

keepalive.description: False creates the run with the keepalive off: the host does not reopen the loop when the orchestrator stops with ready tasks (default true).

branch.description: Commit on gt/<run> (default) or on the current branch.

shared.description: Registry files, indexes, schemas and central types several tasks touch. jtasks validate warns about two tasks with no dependency between them touching one (in files or touchesShared).

sharedPolicy.description: warn (the default): only the warning; serialize: two tasks touching the same shared file never run at the same time (the frontier holds one back), without the file entering both ownerships.

context.description: The run's context, written once (brief first): the tool renders it at the top of the ## Context section of every ticket (jtasks context --set replaces it later).

what.description: What to build: the end-to-end behaviour this task makes work, from the user's side; no file paths (they go in files) and no code.

source.description: Where this task came from, when it is not the plan's source.

dependsOn.description: Ids of the tasks that block this one.

files.description: Files and folders it owns, relative to the repository; a folder owns everything inside; dir/** is the folder; no other patterns.

acceptance.description: Acceptance criteria: each one observable, false at the commit the task starts from, and made true by this task alone.

boundary.description: Scope boundary: what this task does not do.

exclusive.description: Runs alone. "project" (or true): holds the whole repository. "machine": also waits for every jtasks task on the machine and keeps new ones out (benchmarks, timing tests).

oneOf.description: A jlock resource: desktop, clipboard, browser, audio, gpu, network, machine, port:<n>, or one of the user's (jlock resources lists them).

uses.description: What the task uses besides files, held while it runs so tasks of every run that use it wait for each other; exclusive by default.

touchesShared.description: Files of the plan's shared this task touches without owning them (it claims them when it needs them).

context.description: Only the HOW-relevant knowledge this task alone needs (decisions, interfaces, pitfalls, the code to start from), inlined; never a repeat of what, acceptance, files, boundary, the common brief or the run's context.
The run's context. Each piece of information appears once in a ticket: the brief holds what every task shares; read, consult and constraints here are only for what truly applies to every task.

brief.description: Path of the Markdown file with the common brief (absolute, or relative to the cwd): the problem, the goal, the decisions and the shared conventions and interfaces every task needs, distilled from the plan, inlined. The tool keeps its text as brief.md in the run's folder (write it there directly: the path plan --draft prints) and puts it verbatim at the top of every ticket's ## Context. A missing or empty file is a plan error.

summary.description: 0.5 form, kept for old plans: a short paragraph every ticket shows. Prefer brief.

read.description: Files every task must read before starting (keep it minimal, usually empty): absolute paths, or relative to the repository; may name a section (file.md#heading).

consult.description: Documents every task may open only in case of doubt.

constraints.description: Standing rules every task follows, when they are not already in the brief.

taskContext.description: A task's exclusive context, rendered after the common brief.

summary.description: The facts this task needs to act without researching, short and precise: decisions, interfaces, pitfalls, which existing code to start from. Not a restatement of what.

read.description: Required reading only when it cannot reasonably be inlined (e.g. source code to port); may name a section (file.md#heading).

consult.description: Documents to open only in case of doubt, each with the reason; rendered as If in doubt, consult.

constraints.description: A rule only this task follows.

path.description: Absolute, or relative to the repository; may name a section (file.md#heading).

why.description: Short reason: in which doubt to open it.
